toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change that cut agents' in-call credit limit from £100 to £25. Larger adjustments are now blocked and automatically referred to the Billing Resolution team. The share of billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% that same week. Referred calls resolve at about 33%, and non-referred calls are unchanged at 82%. Billing FCR dropped from 79% to 56%.

The new starters are not the cause. Their referral rate matches tenured agents', and tenured agents' FCR fell by the same amount, from about 75% to 67%. The tariff mix shift is small, and tariff calls still resolve at 85%. The IVR change came two weeks after the drop. I'm fairly confident in this, though I didn't test workload directly.

Don't put the April intake on performance plans. The drop is not their doing and the plan would punish the wrong people. Instead, agree a revised credit authority with Finance and trial it on two teams for six weeks with post-call sampling. The Finance controller has already said they would consider this. Track FCR and unsupported credits. Don't pause the IVR work on this evidence. A dashboard rebuild is useful but not urgent. MI can run the breakdown by team within a day.
